report.source_text: The biopsy showed infiltration by sheets of atypical plasmacytoid cells with some multinucleated forms. Skeletal muscle was also seen. There was no lung parenchyma. Immunohistochemical staining demonstrated that this population was positive for CD138 and MUM1 and weakly positive for CD56. TTF1, p63, S100, AE1/AE3, CD3, CD20 and CD79a were negative. Ki67 was remarkably high (90%). Further immunostains performed at King’s College Hospital reference laboratory revealed that CD38 was strongly positive, there was lambda light chain restriction seen on the immunostaining as well as ISH. Cyclin d1, CD45, pancytokeratin and kappa were negative. Epstein-Barr virus encoded small nuclear RNAs was negative.

A mild to moderate left-sided pleural effusion was noted. CT evidence of lumbar vertebral and pelvic bony metastatic appearances was also seen.

report.source_text: In light of the results of lung biopsy, myeloma screen and bone marrow aspirate and trephine were carried out. Immunoglobulin studies showed a slightly low IgA level of 0.62 g/L with a normal IgM level. Protein electrophoresis demonstrated the presence of 2 g/L of paraprotein consisting of IgG lambda paraprotein and lambda light chains. Light chain studies showed a normal free kappa concentration of 6.12 mg/L and an elevated free lambda concentration of 1178.1. His kappa/lambda ratio was reduced at 0.01. Bone marrow aspirate, trephine and immunophenotyping showed no evidence of infiltration by myeloma. Routine viral serology was negative for hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV 1/2.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old man presented with chest pain, back pain, abdominal distention, and neurological symptoms indicative of spinal cord compression. Initial clinical suspicion was lung cancer. Lung biopsy revealed sheets of atypical plasmacytoid cells positive for CD138, MUM1, CD38, with lambda light chain restriction, consistent with plasmablastic myeloma (E006). Imaging showed a large lung mass invading the chest wall, with bony metastatic lesions including vertebral involvement and thoracic spinal cord compression (E005, E003). Laboratory studies demonstrated IgG lambda paraprotein and abnormal serum free lambda light chains, but no bone marrow infiltration was found (E007).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Lung biopsy shows plasmablastic myeloma with immunophenotypic positivity for CD138, MUM1, CD38, and lambda light chain restriction
Chest CT shows a large lobular lung mass with chest wall invasion and bony metastases
Spinal MRI reveals widespread skeletal metastases and thoracic spinal cord compression
Serum studies demonstrate IgG lambda paraprotein and elevated free lambda light chains; bone marrow biopsy negative for infiltration

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Histopathology did not show epithelial markers, was negative for TTF1 and pancytokeratin; features consistent with plasmablastic myeloma instead
